questions.prompt: Who will check the dashboard at the start, and who marks a report as cleared: your team or the council's staff?
questions.why: This tells me who needs a login.
questions.note: Answered by email on 20 September: each council sees only its own area, a Resolve view sees everything, and councils can acknowledge, schedule and clear but not verify.

questions.prompt: How do you plan to approach a council, and do you have a contact or a way in?
questions.why: Reports only get fixed if a council takes part.
questions.note: Answered by email on 20 September: councils and contractors will be approached once there's a prototype that looks good and works, and you can usually get a meeting.

questions.prompt: What is the plan for testing Resolve UK?
questions.why: This helps me decide where to start.

questions.prompt: Should a report count as verified after 5 people agree, each with a photo, and who should check each photo: the AI, a Resolve reviewer, or both?
questions.why: This sets how much checking falls on your team, and what "verified" means in the figures.

questions.prompt: If someone disagrees and sends a photo, should a Resolve reviewer check it and send the report back to the council if it's right?
questions.why: Some people disagree just to be difficult, so a single complaint shouldn't reopen a fix.

questions.prompt: In a remote area where 5 residents may never reply, should a Resolve reviewer be able to verify a fix from one clear photo?
questions.why: Otherwise a fix in a quiet area could stay unverified forever.

questions.prompt: Colchester has two levels of council, so a report there may need routing to two places. Are you happy to start there, or should Huddersfield go first?
questions.why: Two levels means two routes to set up, which is a little more work. The plan already allows for it, and I still need to check who covers what.

decisions.title: Where the data is hosted
decisions.outcome: In the UK (London). The data moves before any real reports come in.
decisions.detail: The prototype's test data is in Seoul for now.

decisions.title: What each council can see
decisions.outcome: Each council sees only the reports for its own area. A Resolve view sees everything.
decisions.detail: For example, London cannot see Manchester's reports.

decisions.title: What councils can do, and what they can't
decisions.outcome: Councils can acknowledge, schedule and clear. They cannot verify. Resolve reviewers can verify and see the data, but cannot change what a council has done.

decisions.title: What the pilot is
decisions.outcome: The routing and checking stage is the pilot stage.

decisions.title: What the time measure counts
decisions.outcome: Days until the council marks a report cleared, not until it's verified, so councils in remote areas aren't penalised when a problem was dealt with quickly.

decisions.title: When councils and contractors are approached
decisions.outcome: Once there's a prototype that looks good and works. Ms Kay arranges the meetings.

decisions.title: How many confirmations before a report counts as verified
decisions.detail: Ms Kay suggested 5. To confirm: 5 agreements, each with a photo?
decisions.needed_by: Before the pilot stage is built

decisions.title: What happens when someone disagrees with a photo
decisions.detail: Proposed: a Resolve reviewer checks it and sends the report back to the council if it's right. Disagreeing without a photo does nothing.
decisions.needed_by: Before the pilot stage is built

decisions.title: Remote areas where 5 residents may never reply
decisions.detail: Proposed: a Resolve reviewer can verify from one clear photo.

updates.title: First working prototype
updates.summary: Report a problem with a photo, a category and a location, and see it in a list. It installs on a phone like an app.
updates.details_md:
You can now:

- Open the prototype on a phone and add it to the home screen.
- Report a problem: pick a type, describe it, add a photo, and mark the location using the phone or a map pin.
- See every report in a list with its photo and status.

Every report shows "Reported" for now, because no council is connected yet.

updates.title: Cleaner design and branding
updates.summary: A more modern look with light and dark modes, the Resolve logo and app icons, and a map that works from anywhere.
updates.details_md:
What changed:

- A cleaner layout with a simpler form, clearer buttons and a dropdown that looks the same on every device.
- Light and dark modes that follow the phone's setting.
- The Resolve logo in the header, and proper app icons for the home screen.
- The map opens on a world view, so it works wherever someone is.

updates.title: Blueprint, first version

updates.details_md: Covers how a report moves from a phone to a confirmed fix, what gets built and in what order, rough timings, and your questions answered.

updates.title: Blueprint updated with your answers
updates.summary: Your decisions from 20 September are now in the plan.
updates.details_md:
What changed:

- **Hosting.** UK hosting is decided.
- **Who can do what.** Councils see only their own area and can acknowledge, schedule and clear, but not verify. A Resolve view sees everything and can verify without changing what a council did.
- **How a fix is checked.** The public is shown that a report is cleared and asked whether they agree, with a photo. Disagreeing without a photo doesn't send it back. Five confirmations is the draft rule.
- **The pilot.** Routing and checking fixes is now called out as the pilot stage.
- **Measuring councils.** The measure stops at "cleared", not "verified".
- **The AI step.** The diagram now says it is the AI being confident in its suggestion.
- **Decisions.** The decisions that can wait now have their own page, so they aren't forgotten.
